newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Storm weakens off Bangladesh coast.
newsitem.headline: Storm weakens off Bangladesh coast.

text.p: A cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal remained stationary 600 km (370 miles) from Bangladesh coast, but has weakened, meteorology officials said on Monday.
Danger warning signals at all ports, including Chittagong, have been lowered, they said.

The Storm Warning Centre in Dhaka said in its latest bulletin at 12 noon (0600 GMT) that "latest satellite imagery indicates that the cyclonic storm over east-central and north Bay has apparently weakened into a well-marked low".
Meteorology officials in Chittagong, Mongla and Cox's Bazar -- all threatened by the storm -- said the sky was clearing of thick cloud and the sun had reappeared after two days.
Normal activities have resumed at Chittagong port and ships that were moved to the outer anchorage on Sunday have started retuning to jetties, port officials said.
"It seems the danger is over although we are still expecting some wind blasts and rain," a Cox's Bazar official told Reuters.
